summary: Qualify shared runtime preferences through two actual installed MCP processes and a restart, integrate the proof into package verification, and extend isolated managed-Codex configuration discovery without changing runtime authority.
decisions: Keep DCP-016 verification independent from the DCP-010 runtime replacement repair. The initial standalone probe used its packed candidate; identify actual product bytes with recorded installed module hashes.
Require the canonical installed bin under the explicitly supplied owned installation prefix and verify package name/version/bin before launch. Reject source and mismatched-package substitutions.

Exercise request-by-request reload through native/compatible/multi-file reads, warning thresholds and exact bytes, repeated concurrent distinct-key writes, root restrictions, invalid values, command blocks, corrupt-policy cleanup and restart persistence.

Use a fixture-owned hard-deny preload with ten positive canaries. Record attempted Node transport API names before throwing, bound retained attempts and describe its observation scope without claiming an OS sandbox.

Drain bounded stderr, give initialize/list/tool calls five-second deadlines, capture original PIDs before awaiting initialization, and independently observe ESRCH after SDK close. Never kill a numeric PID as an ambiguity fallback.
Keep all configuration and CODEX_HOME state synthetic. Actual Codex agent/model tool invocation remains false. Preserve current local/remote permissions, real auth and staging deployment.

Preserve every broad requirement stage/weight/acceptance/estimate and all 48 DCP issue states. Append scoped evidence and pending-gate limits; update continuation closeout fields only from actual final results.
